purpose: Skeleton-first shoulder-girdle geometry audit. Test the a003 mesh-driven clavicle/scapula spans against independent osseous morphometry.

scapula_longitudinal_length_predicted_fr.definition: study longitudinal scapular length; exact landmark mapping must be checked before comparing to GH-to-inferior-angle

ANSUR_stature_conditioned_biacromial_bre.definition: bony biacromial breadth at the acromia; AC joints lie medial to the lateral acromial points

findings: Independent global breadth check: a003 bi-AC joint breadth is ~481.4 mm, while stature-conditioned ANSUR male biacromial breadth is ~425.2±16.2 mm. Because each AC joint lies medial to the lateral acromial point, bi-AC breadth should be smaller than biacromial breadth; a003 is already ~3.47 residual SD above the expected biacromial mean. This independently confirms excessive lateral shoulder-girdle width without relying on a clavicle-length study.

The a003 clavicle SC-to-AC straight span (~223 mm) is anatomically implausible. It exceeds a male CT true curved clavicle mean (~150 mm) by ~73 mm and even exceeds a male cadaver 3D centreline mean (~167 mm) by ~56 mm. A straight endpoint chord cannot legitimately be longer than the true curved bone length.

Scapular size evidence is method-sensitive. One dry-bone male sample reports height ~148 mm, while an Italian male CT stature equation predicts longitudinal scapular length ~207.8 mm at 1.82 m. Because a003 uses GH-to-inferior-angle (~212 mm), none of these are endpoint-identical. The scapula is therefore REOPEN for landmark-compatible 3D reconstruction, but its exact shortening is explicitly NOT confirmed.

The clavicle defect is directly confirmed by measurement semantics; the scapular evidence is conflicting by method and requires landmark-compatible 3D retargeting before either shortening or retention is claimed.

The previously corroborated GH depth relative to the acromion does not rescue the overall shoulder-girdle proportions. Local joint-depth placement can be reasonable while the global SC-AC and scapular spans are wrong.
The final skeleton-first shoulder must therefore retarget SC, AC, scapular body, acromion and glenoid geometry independently of the r95 shoulder width, then the mesh must be narrowed/refit around it.
canonical_requirements: Use stature-conditioned biacromial breadth as a global outer bony-shoulder scaffold; reconstructed bilateral AC joints must lie medial to the acromial endpoints.

Define scapular superior angle, inferior angle, medial border/spine root, acromion, coracoid and glenoid centre from an evidence-backed local scapular frame before selecting any GH-to-inferior target.
Represent clavicle with a curved centreline or equivalent non-bone reference geometry; SC and AC remain true endpoints.
Use male clavicle endpoint/centreline corridors and preserve the fact that endpoint distance must be shorter than curved true length.
Keep AC and GH centres distinct and anatomically separated.
After girdle retargeting, recompute shoulder breadth from skeleton plus realistic deltoid/soft-tissue thickness rather than preserving the old mesh breadth.
acceptance_tests: Bilateral AC-joint breadth is less than bilateral lateral-acromion (biacromial) breadth and both are checked against the stature-conditioned global shoulder-width corridor.
SC-to-AC endpoint distance is less than the corresponding clavicle curved centreline length.
Clavicle centreline and endpoint measures fall inside a multi-source adult male corridor or have a documented stature-specific justification.
Scapular GH-to-inferior-angle distance must be checked against a landmark-compatible 3D scapular envelope (height + width + glenoid position), not against height alone.
Glenoid size/orientation and glenoid-to-acromion relationship remain within source corridors.
Bilateral mirror symmetry is preserved in the canonical skeleton.
Shoulder-complex movement tests are rerun because changing SC/AC/scapular geometry changes GH path and lever arms.

audit_correction_2026_10_08.reason: Earlier wording treated GH-to-inferior-angle distance as if it must be less than superior-to-inferior scapular height. That is not a valid hard invariant because GH is laterally offset; the Euclidean span can exceed vertical height.
audit_correction_2026_10_08.correction: Use a 3D height/width/glenoid-position envelope. Clavicle chord-vs-centreline invariant remains valid.
audit_correction_2026_10_08.result: Scapula remains strongly suspicious but exact shortening is not claimed from a height-only comparison.

additional_crosscheck.effect: Weakens any claim that a003 scapular span is definitely oversized. Exact scapular geometry remains unresolved because measurement endpoints differ.
